statement:
Show that

(i) $\dfrac{1-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}=\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}$;

(ii) if $|k|<1$ then
$$\int\frac{dx}{1-2kx+x^2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x-k}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}\right)+C,$$
where $C$ is a constant of integration.

Hence, or otherwise, show that if $0<\alpha<\pi$ then
$$\int_0^1\frac{\sin\alpha}{1-2x\cos\alpha+x^2}\,dx=\frac{\pi-\alpha}{2}.$$
solution:
(i) Using the double-angle formulae, $1-\cos\alpha=2\sin^2\tfrac{\alpha}{2}$ and $\sin\alpha=2\sin\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\cos\tfrac{\alpha}{2}$, so
$$\frac{1-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}=\frac{2\sin^2\tfrac{\alpha}{2}}{2\sin\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\cos\tfrac{\alpha}{2}}=\tan\tfrac{\alpha}{2}.$$

(ii) Complete the square in the denominator:
$$1-2kx+x^2=(x-k)^2+(1-k^2).$$
Let $u=x-k$. Then $du=dx$ and
$$\int\frac{dx}{1-2kx+x^2}=\int\frac{du}{u^2+(1-k^2)}.$$
Since $|k|<1$, write $a=\sqrt{1-k^2}>0$:
$$\int\frac{du}{u^2+a^2}=\frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{u}{a}+C=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x-k}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}\right)+C.$$

Now for the final integral, set $k=\cos\alpha$ (so $|k|<1$ since $0<\alpha<\pi$). Then $1-2x\cos\alpha+x^2=1-2kx+x^2$ and $\sqrt{1-k^2}=\sqrt{1-\cos^2\alpha}=\sin\alpha$ (positive since $0<\alpha<\pi$). By (ii),
$$\int_0^1\frac{1}{1-2x\cos\alpha+x^2}\,dx=\left[\frac{1}{\sin\alpha}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\right)\right]_0^1.$$

Multiplying by $\sin\alpha$:
$$\int_0^1\frac{\sin\alpha}{1-2x\cos\alpha+x^2}\,dx=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\right).$$

By (i), $\dfrac{1-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}=\tan\tfrac{\alpha}{2}$, and $\dfrac{-\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}=-\cot\alpha=\tan\left(\alpha-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Hence
$$\int_0^1\frac{\sin\alpha}{1-2x\cos\alpha+x^2}\,dx=\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(\alpha-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right).$$

Now $\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\in(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2})$ so $\tan^{-1}(\tan\tfrac{\alpha}{2})=\tfrac{\alpha}{2}$. And $\alpha-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\in(-\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{\pi}{2})$ so $\tan^{-1}(\tan(\alpha-\tfrac{\pi}{2}))=\alpha-\tfrac{\pi}{2}$. Therefore
$$\int_0^1\frac{\sin\alpha}{1-2x\cos\alpha+x^2}\,dx=\frac{\alpha}{2}-\left(\alpha-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi-\alpha}{2}.$$

as required.
hints: For the final integral, take k = cos(alpha) and use sqrt(1-k^2)=sin(alpha).
Use part (i) to simplify tan^{-1} of the endpoints.
